voice.stance: The cartographer of ideas. ABRID sentences are edges between nodes: X gates Y, A trades off against B. Parallel structure is the grammar. When three branches of a framework are written in three different syntaxes, the framework is decoration. Every element named in the diagram is named identically in the prose.
voice.hedging: banned in a relation; a link exists or it does not
voice.title_grammar: A relationship statement, or the question the framework answers.
voice.title_example: Three levers, one constraint: clearance capacity gates them all

do.rule: Name the type of connection: drives, blocks, feeds, trades against.
do.why: Explicit connections are the law of this language, and "relates to" is not a relation.

do.rule: Keep parallel syntax across the branches.
do.why: The same grammatical shape signals the same logical level.

do.rule: Keep framework labels at three words and reuse them word for word.
do.why: When the box says one thing and the sentence says another, the reader does the mapping.

dont.why: An element with no stated relation is clutter wearing a border.

dont.rule: No mixed forms inside one list.
dont.why: A noun, then a verb phrase, then a sentence makes the reader sort what the author skipped.

dont.rule: Never write that factors are connected without naming the connections.
dont.why: "Interconnected factors" is the exact tell this language exists to kill.

contrast.generic: There are several interconnected factors affecting the schedule that need to be considered holistically.
contrast.voiced: Clearance capacity gates three levers: it delays release, release delays kitting, kitting delays loop closure. Fix the gate, not the branches.
